target_customer: Indian startups, SMEs and enterprises that accept online payments, then also payouts, business banking, payroll and lending
problem: In 2014 getting an online payment gateway in India was slow and cumbersome with poor developer tools, so Razorpay offered quick onboarding and developer friendly APIs.
business_model: Payment processing take rate on transactions, plus SaaS and lending revenue from banking, payroll and credit products

founders.name: Harshil Mathur
founders.background_notes: Worked in the Middle East for Schlumberger per YC interview.

founders.name: Shashank Kumar
founders.background_notes: Worked at Microsoft in the USA before the startup.

competitors.name: PayU India
competitors.traction_then: Named as a main rival in 2015 Series A coverage; blogs describe older gateways as cumbersome
competitors.funding_then: Part of larger group, not stated

competitors.name: CCAvenue
competitors.traction_then: Listed with Paytm, PayU and PayPal in 2016 coverage

competitors.name: Instamojo
competitors.what: Payment tool focused on individual sellers

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a reliable gateway with bank integrations and fraud controls is standard engineering with hard operational parts: uptime, bank relationships and compliance with Indian regulation.

defensibility.rationale: RBI licenses, bank integrations and merchant switching costs help, but gateways are largely interchangeable and competitors copied features; breadth of products added stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents and new rivals like Cashfree and PhonePe kept competing, but Razorpay grew into a multi product unicorn valued at $7.5B in December 2021 and prepared an Indian IPO.

market_need_then: Founders hit problems with existing gateways while building a donation platform in 2014. Contemporary coverage described old gateways as hard to start on for startups and SMEs, with growth in Indian e-commerce.

branding.domain_note: Uses razorpay.com as primary domain; history not found

identity.logo: Blue mark reported by logo sites to signal sharp focus; meaning is not confirmed by the founders
identity.voice_and_tone: Developer friendly, positioned as built for developers by developers

branding.brand_signature: Developer friendly APIs and the claim of being India's full stack financial solutions company
branding.community_and_virality: Won Startup of the Year at the ET Startup Awards 2022; widely used by unicorn startups, which the company says is 76 of 100.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong awareness in Indian startup and developer circles and a trusted payments name, though most evidence is the company's own claims.

pivots.from: Crowdfunding or donation platform for India
pivots.to: Payment gateway for startups and SMEs
pivots.why: Founders found that setting up online payment gateways was cumbersome

outcome_analysis: Razorpay won by making online payments easy for Indian startups with developer friendly products, then expanded into banking, payroll, lending and acquisitions. It raised from Tiger Global, Sequoia, GIC and others, reaching a $7.5B valuation in December 2021, and moved its domicile back to India in 2025 with an IPO approved by SEBI. Growth rode UPI and digital payment adoption while competition from other gateways stayed intense.
notes: A Series A was announced in October 2015 per a YourStory headline but the amount and investors were not retrieved, so it is omitted as a round. The 2018 Series B at $20M led by Tiger Global comes from Clay and a search snippet and conflicts with an aggregator listing $100M; unverified. Series C is $75M per several outlets. Series E date is April or October 2021 depending on source. Total raised is $741.5M per company and Entrackr, $816.4M per Clay. Reverse flip completed in 2025; FY25 loss of INR 1,209 crore attributed to one time costs. SEBI approval for IPO reported November 2026 per YC page headline; the company has not listed as of this research. Competitors are from 2015 and early 2016 coverage.
